heading: INT. COMMUNITY POOL - SHALLOW END - DAY

units.text: INT. COMMUNITY POOL - SHALLOW END - DAY
Chlorine glare.
A lifeguard chair.
A ring of damp kickboards.
A sign: NO RUNNING, NO DIVING, NO FUN.
SEVEN-YEAR-OLD PENELOPE ABERNATHY floats in a swan-shaped tube, arms folded, as stern as a dowager.
Her father TOBIAS ABERNATHY, forties, wades beside her in cargo shorts and sunglasses.
Her aunt CORDELIA, fifties, sits on the pool edge with her feet in the water, reading a paperback.
Two teenage lifeguards, DYLAN KOWALSKI and MARISOL DUARTE, share the chair, both pretending not to watch.
And a gray-haired swimmer, MR. PEMBERTON-LEE, seventy, does a slow, magisterial breaststroke past them.
The swan tube drifts.
Tobias catches it with a finger, steering it back.
Penelope looks at him with great disdain.
Cordelia turns a page.
Dylan stands up, peers over the pool, sits back down.
Marisol nudges his knee with her elbow.
Mr. Pemberton-Lee reaches the wall, touches it, and pivots, unhurried.
The swan tube squeaks.
Penelope presses her lips together and does not cry.
Tobias lifts his sunglasses and then lowers them.
Cordelia folds the corner of her page and sets the paperback beside her on the tiles.
Without a word, she slides into the water and wades over.
She takes the other side of the tube, and together she and Tobias walk it toward the steps while Penelope, captain of the swan, sails between them, chin high.
